name: quote-expiry
description: Flow 10. The quote_validity_expiry per-entity timer (contract artefact 5 concern "quote-expire", name quote-expire:<quoteId>). A wake-up, not a decision: it re-reads every decision on the quote and every policy carrying that quote_id, and lapses only an OPEN, unsuperseded decision whose quote_validity_expiry has passed with no bind — a bound quote is proved twice over (a policy record, or a BOUND/ISSUED decision) and is never lapsed. The lapse is APPEND-ONLY per contract artefact 3: a new decision instance carrying origin_flow flow-10 and supersedes_decision_id records it, and the expiring instance gains decision_status SUPERSEDED plus the superseded_by forward pointer, so it leaves the decision_status:OPEN referral queue. It then moves the referral task filed under that decision id to "lapsed" (contract artefact 4 status 7), never touching one a person has already approved or declined. It deliberately does NOT write quote_outcome_config: that record is materialised by the return projection (plan 1.5), not by a publisher flow. Timer payload: {quote_id, decision_id?}. NOTE: nothing schedules this concern yet — artefact 5 A5-3 leaves the storing record open and decision_config has no quote_expire_timer_topic property.

static.note_a5_3: The flow is named quote-expiry (artefact 5 registers the CONCERN token as quote-expire). The concern token and the flow name are different strings by design: the topic is <flowTopic>.<hash(name)>, so the flow name decides the namespace and the concern token is the second line of defence.
static.note_gap: decision_config has no quote_expire_timer_topic property, so a scheduler cannot yet satisfy ASSERT-2a for this concern. Artefact 1 and artefact 5 A5-3 must settle the storing record before anything books this timer.
